addPhone.titleOne.description: Heading of the card that lets a person waiting for access join at once by adding a phone number, when one community invited them. {{community}} is that community's name. Join is a verb.

addPhone.titleSeveral.description: Heading of the card that lets a person waiting for access join at once by adding a phone number, when several communities invited them. "Them" is those communities, named in the sentence just above.

addPhone.lead.text: Add your phone number and you’re in, no waiting. The group sees your name, never your number.
addPhone.lead.description: Explanation under the heading of the add-your-phone card on the waiting screen. "The group" is the community the person was invited to.

addPhone.numberLabel.description: Label of the phone number field on the card that asks for a phone number so a person on the waitlist can join right away, or so an account can be verified.

addPhone.send.description: Button on the card that asks for a phone number so a person on the waitlist can join right away, or so an account can be verified: sends a verification code to the phone number by text message (SMS). Text is a verb.

addPhone.sending.description: Shown on that button, disabled, while the text message with the code is being sent.

addPhone.sendFailed.description: Error on the card that asks for a phone number so a person on the waitlist can join right away, or so an account can be verified, when the server refused to send the verification text and gave no reason of its own.

addPhone.networkError.description: Error on the card that asks for a phone number so a person on the waitlist can join right away, or so an account can be verified, when the request did not reach the server.

addPhone.codeTitle.description: Heading of the same card after the code was sent. Texts are text messages (SMS).

addPhone.codeSent.text: We sent a 6-digit code to the number ending {{lastDigits}}.
addPhone.codeSent.description: Explanation under "Check your texts". {{lastDigits}} is the last four digits of the phone number the person typed.

addPhone.codeLabel.description: Label of the field for the 6-digit verification code received by text message.

addPhone.codeMissing.text: Enter the code from the text
addPhone.codeMissing.description: Error shown when the person pressed Continue with the code field empty. "The text" is the text message (SMS) just sent.

addPhone.codeRejected.description: Error shown when the server refused the verification code and gave no reason of its own.

addPhone.verify.description: Button under the code field on the card that asks for a phone number so a person on the waitlist can join right away, or so an account can be verified: checks the code and, if it is right, finishes.

addPhone.checking.description: Shown on that Continue button, disabled, while the code is being checked.

addPhone.changeNumber.description: Link under the code field: goes back to type a different phone number.

addPhone.resend.description: Link under the code field: sends another verification code to the same phone number.

addPhone.resendTooSoon.text: Wait a minute before asking for a new code.
addPhone.resendTooSoon.description: Error shown when the person pressed "Send a new code" less than a minute after the last one was sent.

phone.country.description: Accessible name of the country picker in front of a phone number field. It sets the country calling code.

phone.loadFailed.description: Error under a phone number field when the part of the page that checks phone numbers could not be downloaded and the number as typed is not a full international number.

phone.missing.description: Error under a phone number field when it was submitted empty.

phone.notANumber.text: That doesn't look like a phone number. Check the digits after the +.
phone.notANumber.description: Error under a phone number field when the person typed a number starting with + that cannot be read as an international number. Keep the + sign.

phone.notUsMobile.text: That doesn't look like a US mobile number.
phone.notUsMobile.description: Error under a phone number field when the number typed is not a possible number for the United States.

phone.notUkMobile.text: That doesn't look like a UK mobile number.
phone.notUkMobile.description: Error under a phone number field when the number typed is not a possible number for the United Kingdom.

phone.notMobileIn.text: That doesn't look like a mobile number in {{country}}.
phone.notMobileIn.description: Error under a phone number field when the number typed is not a possible number for the chosen country. {{country}} is the country's name, already in the device's language.

story.welcome.description: Small heading above the headline on the first screen a signed-out visitor sees. Homeroom is the product's name.

story.headline.text: On Homeroom, communities make apps together.
story.headline.description: Headline on the first screen a signed-out visitor sees: what the product is, in one sentence. Homeroom is the product's name.

story.examples.description: Small heading over a short list of example apps a community might make, under the headline of the signed-out first screen.

story.start.description: Main button on the signed-out first screen: opens the sheet where a new person makes an account.

story.haveAccount.description: Line under the Get started button on the signed-out first screen. The part in <0></0> is a link that opens the sign-in sheet.

nativeDetails.open.description: Link under a sign-in error inside the Homeroom phone app: opens a dialog with technical details about why the secure sign-in could not start.

nativeDetails.title.description: Title of the dialog with technical details about a failed sign-in inside the Homeroom phone app.

nativeDetails.copy.description: Button in the secure sign-in details dialog: copies the technical report to the clipboard so it can be sent to support.

nativeDetails.copied.description: Confirmation beside the Copy details button after the technical report was copied to the clipboard.

nativeDetails.copyFailed.text: Could not copy. You can select the details below.
nativeDetails.copyFailed.description: Shown beside the Copy details button when copying to the clipboard failed. The report is in a box below, where its text can be selected by hand.

nativeDetails.bridge.blockedFrame.text: The app refused this page’s secure connection. The page origin may differ from the one this app build trusts, but this report cannot confirm the cause.
nativeDetails.bridge.blockedFrame.description: Explanation at the top of the secure sign-in details dialog. "The app" is the Homeroom phone app that wraps this web page; "page origin" is the web address the page was loaded from.

nativeDetails.bridge.unattached.text: The app did not answer the secure connection request.
nativeDetails.bridge.unattached.description: Explanation at the top of the secure sign-in details dialog. "The app" is the Homeroom phone app that wraps this web page.

nativeDetails.bridge.inconclusive.text: The app’s connection check did not return a conclusive answer.
nativeDetails.bridge.inconclusive.description: Explanation at the top of the secure sign-in details dialog. "The app" is the Homeroom phone app that wraps this web page.

nativeDetails.bridge.unsupported.text: This app build does not support the secure connection this page needs.
nativeDetails.bridge.unsupported.description: Explanation at the top of the secure sign-in details dialog. "App build" is the installed version of the Homeroom phone app.

nativeDetails.bridge.ready.text: The bridge connected, but native login preparation still failed.
nativeDetails.bridge.ready.description: Explanation at the top of the secure sign-in details dialog, for support staff. "The bridge" is the technical link between the web page and the Homeroom phone app.

nativeDetails.bridge.unknown.text: The bridge has not reported a connection result.
nativeDetails.bridge.unknown.description: Explanation at the top of the secure sign-in details dialog, for support staff. "The bridge" is the technical link between the web page and the Homeroom phone app.

session.failure.rejected.text: Sign-in was accepted, but the server did not recognise your session. Check that this browser allows cookies for Homeroom, then retry the session check.
session.failure.rejected.description: Notice on a sign-in screen after the password or code was accepted but the session could not be confirmed. "Retry the session check" refers to the button below, labelled "Retry session check". Homeroom is the product's name.

session.failure.serverResponse.text: Sign-in was accepted, but the server could not confirm your session. Wait a moment, then retry the session check.
session.failure.serverResponse.description: Notice on a sign-in screen after the password or code was accepted but the session could not be confirmed. "Retry the session check" refers to the button below, labelled "Retry session check".

session.failure.network.text: Sign-in was accepted, but we could not reach the server to confirm your session. Check your connection, then retry the session check.
session.failure.network.description: Notice on a sign-in screen after the password or code was accepted but the session could not be confirmed. "Retry the session check" refers to the button below, labelled "Retry session check".

session.failure.timeout.text: Sign-in was accepted, but confirming your session took too long. Check your connection, then retry the session check.
session.failure.timeout.description: Notice on a sign-in screen after the password or code was accepted but the session could not be confirmed. "Retry the session check" refers to the button below, labelled "Retry session check".

session.failure.invalidResponse.text: Sign-in was accepted, but the session response could not be read. Retry the session check. If it keeps failing, copy the details for support.
session.failure.invalidResponse.description: Notice on a sign-in screen after the password or code was accepted but the session could not be confirmed. "Retry the session check" refers to the button below, labelled "Retry session check". "Copy the details" refers to the Copy details button in the same notice.

session.failure.client.text: Your session could not be opened on this device. Retry the session check. If it keeps failing, copy the details for support.
session.failure.client.description: Notice on a sign-in screen after the password or code was accepted but the session could not be confirmed. "Retry the session check" refers to the button below, labelled "Retry session check". "Copy the details" refers to the Copy details button in the same notice.

session.retry.description: Button on the notice shown when a sign-in was accepted but the session that should follow could not be confirmed: asks the server again whether the person is signed in.

session.checking.description: Shown on the Retry session check button, disabled, while the server is being asked again.

session.details.description: Label of a fold on the notice shown when a sign-in was accepted but the session that should follow could not be confirmed: opens a technical report for support.

session.copy.description: Button under the technical report on the notice shown when a sign-in was accepted but the session that should follow could not be confirmed: copies the report to the clipboard.

session.copied.description: Confirmation under the Copy details button after the sign-in report was copied to the clipboard.

session.copyFailed.text: Could not copy. You can select the details above.
session.copyFailed.description: Shown under the Copy details button when copying to the clipboard failed. The report is in a box above, where its text can be selected by hand.

session.networkError.description: Error on any sign-in or sign-up form when the request did not reach the server.

native.sessionNotPrepared.text: Secure app session could not be prepared. Force-quit and reopen Homeroom, then try again.
native.sessionNotPrepared.description: Error on a sign-in form inside the Homeroom phone app, when the app could not get ready to sign in. Homeroom is the app's name; force-quit means closing the app completely from the phone's app switcher.

native.updateRequired.text: This Homeroom app version must be updated for secure sign-in
native.updateRequired.description: Error on a sign-in form inside the Homeroom phone app, when the installed app is too old to sign in. Homeroom is the app's name.

offline.signIn.text: You're offline. Signing in needs a connection.
offline.signIn.description: Error on a sign-in or sign-up form when the person pressed its button while the device has no internet connection.

signIn.failed.description: Error on the password sign-in form when the server refused the username and password and gave no reason of its own.

register.tagline.text: A place where users own and build apps together
register.tagline.description: Tagline in italics under the name Homeroom at the top of the register screen.

register.lead.description: Line under the tagline at the top of the register screen: says what the form below is for.

register.codeLabel.description: Label of the first field on the register screen, where a person with an activation code makes an account. An activation code is a code an administrator gave the person that lets them register.

register.codePlaceholder.description: Grey placeholder inside the Activation Code field on the register screen. Lower case in English on purpose.

register.usernameLabel.description: Label of the username field on the register screen, where a person with an activation code makes an account.

register.usernamePlaceholder.description: Grey placeholder inside the Username field on the register screen. Lower case in English on purpose.

register.usernamePublic.text: Your username will be public to other users on Homeroom.
register.usernamePublic.description: Note under the Username field on the register screen. Homeroom is the product's name.

register.usernameRule.text: Letters, numbers and underscores, 3 to 32 characters.
register.usernameRule.description: Hint under the Username field on the register screen: what a username may contain and how long it may be.

register.passwordLabel.description: Label of the password field on the register screen, where a person with an activation code makes an account.

register.passwordPlaceholder.description: Grey placeholder inside the Password field on the register screen. Lower case in English on purpose.

register.passwordRule.description: Hint under the Password field on the register screen: the shortest password allowed.

register.submit.description: Main button of the register form: creates the account. A verb.

register.failed.description: Error on the register form when the server refused to create the account and gave no reason of its own.

register.haveAccount.description: Button-shaped link under the register form: goes to the sign-in screen. The part in <0></0> is drawn in the accent colour; the whole line is one link.

verify.vote.title.text: Verify to vote on public apps
verify.vote.title.description: Title on the sheet that asks a person to verify their account before their vote on a public app can count.

verify.vote.lead.text: Votes on public apps count from verified accounts, so each person votes once. Add your phone number to vote now. Nobody sees your number.
verify.vote.lead.description: Explanation under that title when a phone number can be added right there, in the form below it.

verify.vote.reason.text: Votes on public apps count from verified accounts, so each person votes once.
verify.vote.reason.description: Explanation under that title when adding a phone number is not offered and the only way is linking accounts in Settings.

verify.public.title.description: Title on the sheet that asks a person to verify their account before their project can be made public. "It" is the project.

verify.public.lead.text: Public projects need a verified owner, so each person counts once. Add your phone number and it goes public. Nobody sees your number.
verify.public.lead.description: Explanation under "Verify to make it public" when a phone number can be added right there. "It" is the project.

verify.public.reason.text: Public projects need a verified owner, so each person counts once.
verify.public.reason.description: Explanation under "Verify to make it public" when adding a phone number is not offered.

verify.credits.title.description: Title on the sheet that asks a person to verify their account to receive more free AI credits. Verify is a verb.

verify.credits.lead.text: Verified accounts get more free AI credits, so each person counts once. Nobody sees your number.
verify.credits.lead.description: Explanation under "Verify your account" when a phone number can be added right there. AI credits are the allowance spent when an AI builds something for the person.

verify.credits.reason.text: Verified accounts get more free AI credits, so each person counts once.
verify.credits.reason.description: Explanation under "Verify your account" when adding a phone number is not offered.

verify.linkAccountsInstead.text: Or link both GitHub and X in <0>Settings</0>.
verify.linkAccountsInstead.description: Line under the phone number form on the verify sheet: the other way to verify. GitHub and X (the social network) are product names; <0></0> is a link to the linked-accounts page of Settings.

verify.linkAccounts.text: Link both GitHub and X in <0>Settings</0>.
verify.linkAccounts.description: Line on the verify sheet when a phone number cannot be added: the only way to verify. GitHub and X (the social network) are product names; <0></0> is a link to the linked-accounts page of Settings.

verify.notNow.description: Link at the foot of the verify sheet: closes it without verifying.

waiting.title.description: Heading of the screen a person sees after signing up while they do not have access yet.

waiting.lead.text: We let people in a few at a time, and we'll email you when your spot is ready.
waiting.lead.description: Explanation under the heading of the waitlist screen.

waiting.youJoin.text: When you get access, you join {{communities}}.
waiting.youJoin.description: Card on the waitlist screen for a person who followed an invite. {{communities}} is the name of the community they were invited to, or a list of several such names already joined into one phrase ("A, B and C").

waiting.names.pair.description: How two names are joined in the middle of a list of community names on the waitlist screen. {{first}} is everything listed so far and {{second}} the next name. Only the punctuation between them is translated.

waiting.names.last.description: How the last name is added to a list of community names on the waitlist screen, as in "A, B and C". {{names}} is the names before it, already joined; {{last}} is the final name.

waiting.signOut.description: Link at the foot of the waitlist screen: signs the person out of their account.

recaptcha.line.description: Small legal line under a form that sends a phone number. reCAPTCHA and Google are product names. <0></0> links to Google's privacy policy and <1></1> to Google's terms of service. Keep the dots between the parts.

terms.continuing.text: By continuing, you agree to Homeroom's <0>terms</0>.
terms.continuing.description: Small line under the first button of the sign-in sheet. <0></0> is a link to Homeroom's terms of use. Homeroom is the product's name.

terms.signingIn.text: By signing in, you agree to Homeroom's <0>terms</0>.
terms.signingIn.description: Small line under the sign-in buttons on the sign-in screen. <0></0> is a link to Homeroom's terms of use. Homeroom is the product's name.

queue.pending.label.description: Status pill on a waitlist status panel: the person joined the waitlist but has not confirmed their email address yet.

queue.pending.note.text: Click the link in the email we sent, and your answers below move you up.
queue.pending.note.description: Note beside the "Waiting for confirmation" pill. "Your answers below" are the answers to the survey questions under it; "move you up" means a better place on the waitlist.

queue.confirmed.label.description: Status pill on a waitlist status panel and on the Home waitlist card: the person's email address is confirmed and they are waiting for access.

queue.confirmed.note.text: Your address is confirmed. Answering the questions below moves you up.
queue.confirmed.note.description: Note beside the "On the waitlist" pill. Address is the email address; "moves you up" means a better place on the waitlist.

queue.admitted.label.description: Status pill on a waitlist status panel: the person has been given access.

queue.admitted.note.text: Access is open for you. Check your email for the invite.
queue.admitted.note.description: Note beside the "You're in" pill, for a person who has access but has not made an account yet.

queue.admitted.noteLinked.text: Access is open and your account is linked. Sign in any time.
queue.admitted.noteLinked.description: Note beside the "You're in" pill, for a person who has access and already has an account.

invite.dead.expired.text: This invite link has expired. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
invite.dead.expired.description: Shown on the signed-out landing screen in place of the invitation when the invite link the person opened is past its end date.

invite.dead.revoked.text: This invite link was turned off. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
invite.dead.revoked.description: Shown on the signed-out landing screen in place of the invitation when the person who made the invite link cancelled it.

invite.dead.usedUp.text: This invite link has been used as many times as it allows. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
invite.dead.usedUp.description: Shown on the signed-out landing screen in place of the invitation when the invite link has reached its limit of people.

invite.dead.unknown.text: This invite link does not work. Check it was copied whole.
invite.dead.unknown.description: Shown on the signed-out landing screen in place of the invitation when the invite link is not recognised, usually because part of the address is missing.

invite.opening.description: Accessible name of the grey placeholder shown on the landing screen while an invitation is loading.

invite.joinInvitedBy.description: Sentence describing an invitation. {{username}} is the inviter's username, shown after an @ sign that must be kept; {{project}} is the name of the project.

invite.joinInvitedByUnnamed.text: @{{username}} invited you to join a project.
invite.joinInvitedByUnnamed.description: Sentence describing an invitation when the project's name is not known. {{username}} is the inviter's username, shown after an @ sign that must be kept.

invite.joinInvited.description: Sentence describing an invitation when the inviter is not known. {{project}} is the name of the project.

invite.joinInvitedUnnamed.text: You are invited to join a project.
invite.joinInvitedUnnamed.description: Sentence describing an invitation when neither the inviter nor the project's name is known.

invite.invitedBy.description: Line under the project's name on the invitation card of the signed-out landing screen. {{inviter}} is the inviter's display name, or their username with an @; {{project}} is the project's name. No full stop.

invite.invitedByUnnamed.description: Line on the invitation card of the signed-out landing screen when the project's name is not known. {{inviter}} is the inviter's display name, or their username with an @. No full stop.

invite.invited.description: Line under the project's name on the invitation card of the signed-out landing screen when the inviter is not known. {{project}} is the project's name. No full stop.

invite.invitedUnnamed.description: Line on the invitation card of the signed-out landing screen when neither the inviter nor the project's name is known. No full stop.

invite.invitedYouBy.description: Line on the invitation card of the signed-out landing screen, on the layout where the project's name is already written just above. {{inviter}} is the inviter's display name, or their username with an @. No full stop.

invite.invitedYou.description: Line on the invitation card of the signed-out landing screen when the inviter is not known, on the layout where the project's name is already written just above. No full stop.

invite.members_one.description: Second fact on the invitation card's line: how many members the project already has. "It" is the project. No full stop.

invite.members_other.description: Second fact on the invitation card's line: how many members the project already has. "It" is the project. No full stop.

invite.membersSentence_one.description: Sentence saying how many members the project a person is invited to already has. "It" is the project.

invite.membersSentence_other.description: Sentence saying how many members the project a person is invited to already has. "It" is the project.

invite.facts.description: How the two facts on the invitation card's line are joined: {{first}} is who invited the person ("Ada invited you to Game Corner") and {{second}} is how many people are in the project. Only the separator between them is translated.

invite.note.description: The personal note an inviter wrote, on the invitation card. {{inviter}} is the inviter's display name or @username, drawn bold with its colon inside <0></0>; {{note}} is their own words, kept in quotation marks.

invite.noteUnnamed.description: The personal note an inviter wrote, on the invitation card, when the inviter is not known. "They" is that unnamed person, drawn bold with its colon inside <0></0>; {{note}} is their own words, kept in quotation marks.

invite.homeroomLine.text: On Homeroom, people using an app build and improve it together.
invite.homeroomLine.description: One line at the foot of an invitation on the signed-out landing screen that says what Homeroom is. Homeroom is the product's name.

invite.join.description: Main button fixed at the bottom of an invitation on the signed-out landing screen: opens the sheet to make an account and join. Join is a verb; {{project}} is the project's name.

invitePreview.closed.text: Its members, its app and what it is deciding open once you join.
invitePreview.closed.description: Line on the full-page preview of a private community a signed-in person was invited to: its content stays hidden until they join. "Open" is a verb here (become visible), and "its" is the community's.

invitePreview.notNow.description: Accessible name of the back arrow at the top of the invitation preview page: closes the preview without joining.

landing.viewerTitle.description: Accessible title of the frame in which a public app opens on the signed-out landing screen. A noun: the app being used.

landing.tile.accountRequired.description: Small status under an app's tile in the list of public apps on the signed-out landing screen, and the tooltip of its lock badge: the app can only be opened by someone who is signed in.

landing.chips.describe.description: First of four short statements scrolling across the signed-out landing screen that say how Homeroom works. An instruction-like phrase: you describe the app you want in a chat.

landing.chips.build.description: Second of four short statements scrolling across the signed-out landing screen that say how Homeroom works. "It" is the app that was described.

landing.chips.vote.description: Third of four short statements scrolling across the signed-out landing screen that say how Homeroom works: the community accepts the change by voting. "It" is what the AI built.

landing.chips.own.description: Last of four short statements scrolling across the signed-out landing screen that say how Homeroom works: people who contribute to an app own part of it.

landing.appSignInFailed.text: Could not sign in to this app. Check your connection and try again.
landing.appSignInFailed.description: Error toast on the signed-out landing screen when a public app that needs an account could not be opened because signing the person in to it failed.

landing.appOpenFailed.text: This app could not be opened.
landing.appOpenFailed.description: Error toast on the signed-out landing screen when a public app's address is broken and it cannot be opened.

landing.backToApps.description: Accessible name of the back arrow in the header while a public app is open on the signed-out landing screen: closes the app and returns to the landing screen.

landing.offline.title.description: Heading of the notice on the signed-out landing screen while the device has no internet connection.

landing.offline.body.text: Signing in and joining the waitlist both need a connection.
landing.offline.body.description: Body of the offline notice on the signed-out landing screen.

landing.offline.retry.description: Button on the offline notice on the signed-out landing screen: checks again whether the device is connected.

landing.pitch.eyebrow.description: Small upper-case line above the headline on the signed-out landing screen: access to Homeroom is being opened to people little by little.

landing.pitch.headline.text: Come build the next version with us.
landing.pitch.headline.description: Headline on the signed-out landing screen. An invitation; "the next version" is the next version of Homeroom itself.

landing.pitch.body.text: We're letting people in a few at a time, and we'll email you when your spot is ready.
landing.pitch.body.description: Paragraph under the headline on the signed-out landing screen: how the waitlist works.

landing.learnMore.description: Link under the paragraph on the signed-out landing screen: opens Homeroom's public website. Homeroom is the product's name.

landing.joinWaitlist.description: Main button on the signed-out landing screen: opens the form to ask for access. Join is a verb.

landing.signIn.description: Second button on the signed-out landing screen: goes to the sign-in screen.

landing.alreadyJoined.description: Line under the buttons on the signed-out landing screen, for a person who is already on the waitlist. <0></0> is a link to the screen that shows their place.

landing.backToWaiting.description: Button on the signed-out landing screen for a person who is signed in but still waiting for access: returns to their waitlist screen.

landing.sheet.join.description: Title of the sign-in sheet opened from an invitation on the signed-out landing screen. Join is a verb; {{project}} is the name of the project the person was invited to.

landing.sheet.signIn.description: Title of the sign-in sheet when it was opened from the "Sign in" link of the signed-out first screen.

landing.sheet.makeAccount.description: Title of the sign-in sheet when it was opened from the "Get started" button of the signed-out first screen.

more.back.description: Link at the top left of the waitlist survey page: returns to the landing screen. Keep the arrow.

more.eyebrow.description: Small upper-case line above the title of the waitlist survey page: answering is optional and gives a better place on the waitlist.

more.title.description: Title of the waitlist survey page. "In" means being given access to Homeroom.

more.intro.text: Four questions, about three minutes. These are what we read when we pick who gets in next, and you can come back and add to them any time.
more.intro.description: Introduction under the title of the waitlist survey page.

more.registeredWith.description: Small line at the top of the waitlist survey. {{email}} is the email address the person joined the waitlist with, drawn stronger inside <0></0>.

more.throttled.fewMinutes.text: Your link is fine, we’re limiting requests from your address right now. Try again in a few minutes, or just reopen the link from your waitlist email then.
more.throttled.fewMinutes.description: Notice on the waitlist survey page when the server is rate-limiting the person's network address, so the page could not load yet. "Your link" is the personal link from the waitlist email. Used when the wait is not known.

more.throttled.aboutAMinute.text: Your link is fine, we’re limiting requests from your address right now. Try again in about a minute, or just reopen the link from your waitlist email then.
more.throttled.aboutAMinute.description: Notice on the waitlist survey page when the server is rate-limiting the person's network address, so the page could not load yet. "Your link" is the personal link from the waitlist email. Used when the wait is one minute or less.

more.throttled.aboutMinutes_one.text: Your link is fine, we’re limiting requests from your address right now. Try again in about {{count}} minute, or just reopen the link from your waitlist email then.
more.throttled.aboutMinutes_one.description: Notice on the waitlist survey page when the server is rate-limiting the person's network address, so the page could not load yet. "Your link" is the personal link from the waitlist email. {{count}} is the number of minutes to wait; in English it is always 2 or more here.

more.throttled.aboutMinutes_other.text: Your link is fine, we’re limiting requests from your address right now. Try again in about {{count}} minutes, or just reopen the link from your waitlist email then.
more.throttled.aboutMinutes_other.description: Notice on the waitlist survey page when the server is rate-limiting the person's network address, so the page could not load yet. "Your link" is the personal link from the waitlist email. {{count}} is the number of minutes to wait.

more.invalid.text: This link doesn't look right. Use the one from your waitlist email, or <0>join the waitlist</0> first.
more.invalid.description: Notice on the waitlist survey page when the personal link that opened it is not recognised. <0></0> is a link to the landing screen, where a person can join the waitlist.

more.question.description: Small upper-case line above each question of the waitlist survey. {{number}} is the question's position and {{total}} is how many questions there are (4).

more.made.label.description: First question of the waitlist survey: asks for a web address of something the person built or created. Link is a verb here.

more.made.hint.text: A repo, a site, a bot, a mod, a newsletter, a spreadsheet that runs your fantasy league. Built with AI counts, we care that it exists, not how you made it.
more.made.hint.description: Hint under the first question of the waitlist survey: examples of what can be linked. A repo is a code repository; a mod is a modification of a game.

more.made.notePlaceholder.text: What is it, in one line? (optional)
more.made.notePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the short field under the web address in the first question of the waitlist survey: a one-line description of the thing linked.

more.group.label.text: Tell us about a group you’re part of that could use its own app.
more.group.label.description: Second question of the waitlist survey.

more.group.hint.text: A team, a server, a club, a group chat, a co-op, a band, a league, a neighbourhood. Not a hypothetical one, a real group you’re actually in.
more.group.hint.description: Hint under the second question of the waitlist survey: examples of groups. A server is a chat community (for example on Discord).

more.group.placeholder.text: A 200-person Discord for indie game devs in Lagos
more.group.placeholder.description: Example answer shown as the placeholder of the group field in the waitlist survey. Discord is a product name; "a Discord" is a chat community there.

more.group.size.description: First, unselectable option of the drop-down for the size of the group, in the second question of the waitlist survey.

more.group.role.description: First, unselectable option of the drop-down for the person's role in the group, in the second question of the waitlist survey. "It" is the group.

more.group.tools.text: What does it run on today? (pick any)
more.group.tools.description: Label over a row of chips naming tools (chat apps, spreadsheets and so on) the group uses now; several can be picked. "It" is the group.

more.group.needPlaceholder.text: What would its own app do that those tools can't? Money, membership, voting, scheduling, reputation, records…
more.group.needPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the free-text field at the end of the second question of the waitlist survey. "Its" is the group's; "those tools" are the ones picked just above.

more.loss.label.text: Ever had a tool you relied on get killed, paywalled, or ruined?
more.loss.label.description: Third question of the waitlist survey. Killed means shut down; paywalled means it started charging money.

more.loss.hint.text: An app, a platform, a service, a game, a community. The kind of thing that made you look for something like this in the first place.
more.loss.hint.description: Hint under the third question of the waitlist survey. "Something like this" is Homeroom.

more.loss.productPlaceholder.text: Which one? Google Reader, a Discord server, a game's private servers, an API…
more.loss.productPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the field naming the tool that was lost, in the third question of the waitlist survey. Google Reader and Discord are product names.

more.loss.kinds.description: Label over a row of chips naming what happened to the tool (shut down, became paid and so on); several can be picked.

more.loss.storyPlaceholder.text: What happened, and what did you do next? Where did everyone go? Did you move them somewhere? Rebuild it? Give up?
more.loss.storyPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the free-text field at the end of the third question of the waitlist survey.

more.elsewhere.label.description: Fourth question of the waitlist survey: asks for the person's accounts on other networks.

more.elsewhere.hint.text: Connecting an account proves you’re a person with a history, which is most of what gets a signup read quickly. It confirms the account is yours and nothing else, so follow us if you want to, but we won’t claim we checked.
more.elsewhere.hint.description: Hint under the fourth question of the waitlist survey, above buttons that connect a GitHub, X or LinkedIn account. A signup is a waitlist application.

more.connect.start.description: Button in the fourth question of the waitlist survey: opens that service so the person can prove an account there is theirs. Connect is a verb; {{provider}} is GitHub, X or LinkedIn.

more.connect.verified.description: Shown in place of a Connect button once the account was verified. {{provider}} is GitHub, X or LinkedIn and {{account}} the person's account name there. Keep the check mark and the dot.

more.connect.ok.description: Message at the foot of the waitlist survey after the person came back from connecting an account and it worked.

more.connect.unavailable.text: That sign-in is not available yet.
more.connect.unavailable.description: Warning at the foot of the waitlist survey after the person tried to connect an account with a service that is not set up yet.

more.connect.failed.text: Could not verify that account. Please try again.
more.connect.failed.description: Warning at the foot of the waitlist survey after connecting an account failed or was declined.

more.elsewhere.farcaster.description: Placeholder of a field for the person's Farcaster account. Farcaster is a product name; "@handle" shows the expected form, a username after an @.

more.elsewhere.discord.description: Placeholder of a field for the person's Discord account. Discord is a product name.

more.elsewhere.telegram.description: Placeholder of a field for the person's Telegram account. Telegram is a product name; "@handle" shows the expected form, a username after an @.

more.elsewhere.other.description: Placeholder of a free field for accounts on any other network. Twitch, YouTube and Mastodon are product names.

more.follow.link.description: Link in the fourth question of the waitlist survey: opens Homeroom's own profile on that network so the person can follow it. {{network}} is X, LinkedIn or Instagram.

more.follow.done.description: Checkbox under the Follow links in the waitlist survey: the person says they followed Homeroom's profiles.

more.invite.eyebrow.description: Small upper-case line above the last, extra section of the waitlist survey.

more.invite.label.description: Heading of the last section of the waitlist survey, which gives the person a link to invite a friend to the waitlist.

more.invite.hint.text: We try to admit people together. Things are more fun with people you know. Share your link, and if they join we’ll connect your applications so we can try to bring you in together.
more.invite.hint.description: Hint under "Bring someone you’d build with". Applications are waitlist applications; share is a verb.

more.invite.placeholder.description: Placeholder of the read-only field that will hold the person's invite link, while the link is still loading.

more.invite.joined_one.description: Line under the invite link on the waitlist survey. {{count}} is how many people joined the waitlist through the person's link, and {{emails}} is the list of their email addresses. Keep the space before </0>.

more.invite.joined_other.description: Line under the invite link on the waitlist survey. {{count}} is how many people joined the waitlist through the person's link, and {{emails}} is the list of their email addresses. Keep the space before </0>.

more.save.submit.description: Main button of the waitlist survey: sends the answers.

more.save.note.text: A blank answer just means we have less to go on, and nothing here is required.
more.save.note.description: Small note under the Save my answers button of the waitlist survey.

more.save.empty.text: Answer at least one question before saving.
more.save.empty.description: Warning under the Save my answers button when every answer of the waitlist survey is empty.

more.save.failed.description: Error under the Save my answers button when the server refused the answers and gave no reason of its own.

more.save.network.description: Error under the Save my answers button when the request did not reach the server.

more.saved.title.description: Heading shown in place of the waitlist survey after the answers were saved.

more.saved.body.text: These are the answers we actually read when we pick the next group. Your spot is safe either way, and we’ll email you when it opens.
more.saved.body.description: First paragraph after the waitlist survey was saved. "The next group" is the next group of people let in; "it" is the person's spot.

more.saved.later.text: Thought of something later? The link in your waitlist email reopens this form, and answers merge, so nothing you already typed is lost.
more.saved.later.description: Second paragraph after the waitlist survey was saved.

more.saved.edit.description: Button after the waitlist survey was saved: shows the form again with the answers in it.

more.saved.backHome.description: Link after the waitlist survey was saved: returns to the landing screen. Homeroom is the product's name.

signInSheet.resume.cancelled.description: Error on the sign-in sheet after coming back from signing in with Apple or Google, when the person cancelled there.

signInSheet.resume.expired.text: That sign-in took too long, or started somewhere else. Try again.
signInSheet.resume.expired.description: Error on the sign-in sheet after coming back from signing in with Apple or Google, when the attempt timed out or was begun in another browser or tab.

signInSheet.resume.noVerifiedEmail.text: That account has no verified email address to sign in with. Use your email instead.
signInSheet.resume.noVerifiedEmail.description: Error on the sign-in sheet after coming back from signing in with Apple or Google, when the Apple or Google account has no confirmed email address. "Use your email" points to the Continue with email button.

signInSheet.resume.passwordRequired.text: This account signs in with a password. Use "Sign in with a password" below.
signInSheet.resume.passwordRequired.description: Error on the sign-in sheet after coming back from signing in with Apple or Google, when the Homeroom account must use its password. The quoted words are the label of the link below and must match its translation.

signInSheet.resume.adminPasswordRequired.text: This admin account signs in with a password. Use "Sign in with a password" below.
signInSheet.resume.adminPasswordRequired.description: Error on the sign-in sheet after coming back from signing in with Apple or Google, when the account is an administrator's and must use its password. The quoted words are the label of the link below and must match its translation.

signInSheet.resume.linkedElsewhere.text: Your Homeroom account is linked to a different account there. Use your email instead.
signInSheet.resume.linkedElsewhere.description: Error on the sign-in sheet after coming back from signing in with Apple or Google, when the Homeroom account is tied to another Apple or Google account than the one used. "There" is Apple or Google. Homeroom is the product's name.

signInSheet.resume.logoutRequired.text: You are already signed in. Reload the page.
signInSheet.resume.logoutRequired.description: Error on the sign-in sheet after coming back from signing in with Apple or Google, when a session already exists in this browser.

signInSheet.resume.fallback.text: That did not work. Try again, or use your email.
signInSheet.resume.fallback.description: Error on the sign-in sheet after coming back from signing in with Apple or Google, for any failure without a more specific message.

signInSheet.networkError.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when a request did not reach the server.

signInSheet.continueWith.description: Button on the sign-in sheet: signs in or makes an account with that provider. {{provider}} is Apple or Google.

signInSheet.continueWithEmail.description: Button on the sign-in sheet, under the Apple and Google buttons: goes to the step that asks for an email address.

signInSheet.toPhone.text: New to Homeroom? Join with your phone
signInSheet.toPhone.description: Link on the sign-in sheet for a person without an account: goes to the step that asks for a phone number. Homeroom is the product's name.

signInSheet.withPassword.description: Link under the first button of the sign-in sheet: goes to the username and password step. Other messages quote this label.

signInSheet.or.description: Word in the middle of a horizontal divider on the sign-in sheet, between the phone number form and the Apple and Google buttons.

signInSheet.choose.lead.text: Sign in to the account you have.
signInSheet.choose.lead.description: Line under the sheet's title on the step that offers Apple, Google and email, when the person came there from the phone step.

signInSheet.email.lead.description: Line under the sheet's title on the step that asks for an email address.

signInSheet.email.label.description: Label of the email address field on the sign-in sheet.

signInSheet.email.send.description: Button under the email field on the sign-in sheet: emails a 6-digit sign-in code to that address.

signInSheet.email.sending.description: Shown on the Send code button, disabled, while the email with the code is being sent.

signInSheet.email.otherWays.description: Link under the email step of the sign-in sheet: goes back to the Apple and Google buttons.

signInSheet.email.invalid.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when the email field is empty or has no @.

signInSheet.email.tooMany.text: Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.
signInSheet.email.tooMany.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when too many email codes were asked for in a short time and the server gave no message of its own.

signInSheet.email.sendFailed.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when the email with the code could not be sent and the server gave no reason of its own.

signInSheet.code.title.description: Title of the sign-in sheet on the step that asks for the code that was emailed.

signInSheet.code.lead.text: We sent a 6-digit code to {{email}}. It expires in 10 minutes.
signInSheet.code.lead.description: Line under "Check your email". {{email}} is the address the person typed.

signInSheet.code.label.description: Label of the field for the 6-digit code received by email, on the sign-in sheet.

signInSheet.code.submit.description: Button under the emailed-code field on the sign-in sheet: checks the code and signs the person in.

signInSheet.code.checking.description: Shown on that Continue button, disabled, while the emailed code is being checked.

signInSheet.code.changeEmail.description: Link under the emailed-code field: goes back to type a different email address.

signInSheet.code.resend.description: Link under the emailed-code field: emails another code to the same address.

signInSheet.code.resendIn_one.description: The Send a new code link while it is disabled: counts down the seconds until another email code may be asked for. {{count}} is seconds; "s" is the abbreviation for seconds.

signInSheet.code.resendIn_other.description: The Send a new code link while it is disabled: counts down the seconds until another email code may be asked for. {{count}} is seconds; "s" is the abbreviation for seconds.

signInSheet.code.missing.text: Enter the code from the email
signInSheet.code.missing.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when Continue was pressed with the emailed-code field empty.

signInSheet.code.passwordAccount.text: This account signs in with its password.
signInSheet.code.passwordAccount.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when the emailed code was right but the account is one that must sign in with a password.

signInSheet.code.tooManyAttempts.text: Too many code attempts. Try again shortly.
signInSheet.code.tooManyAttempts.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when wrong email codes were entered too many times and the server gave no message of its own.

signInSheet.code.rejected.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when the emailed code was refused and the server gave no reason of its own.

signInSheet.phone.nameLabel.description: Label of the name field on the phone step of the sign-in sheet: the name the group will see for the person.

signInSheet.phone.numberLabel.description: Label of the phone number field on the sign-in sheet.

signInSheet.phone.send.description: Button on the phone step of the sign-in sheet: sends a verification code to the number by text message (SMS). Text is a verb.

signInSheet.phone.sending.description: Shown on the Text me a code button, disabled, while the text message is being sent.

signInSheet.phone.haveAccount.text: Already on Homeroom? <0>Sign in with email</0>
signInSheet.phone.haveAccount.description: Line at the foot of the phone step of the sign-in sheet, for a person who has an account. <0></0> is a link to the email step. Homeroom is the product's name.

signInSheet.phone.nameMissing.description: Error on the phone step of the sign-in sheet when the name field is empty.

signInSheet.phone.nameTooLong_one.text: Your name can be up to {{count}} character.
signInSheet.phone.nameTooLong_one.description: Error on the phone step of the sign-in sheet when the name typed is too long. {{count}} is the longest length allowed (40).

signInSheet.phone.nameTooLong_other.text: Your name can be up to {{count}} characters.
signInSheet.phone.nameTooLong_other.description: Error on the phone step of the sign-in sheet when the name typed is too long. {{count}} is the longest length allowed (40).

signInSheet.phone.tooMany.text: Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.
signInSheet.phone.tooMany.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when too many text-message codes were asked for in a short time and the server gave no message of its own.

signInSheet.phone.sendFailed.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when the text message with the code could not be sent and the server gave no reason of its own.

signInSheet.phoneCode.title.description: Title of the sign-in sheet on the step that asks for the code sent by text message. Texts are text messages (SMS).

signInSheet.phoneCode.lead.text: We sent a 6-digit code to the number ending {{lastDigits}}.
signInSheet.phoneCode.lead.description: Line under "Check your texts" on the sign-in sheet. {{lastDigits}} is the last four digits of the phone number.

signInSheet.phoneCode.label.description: Label of the field for the 6-digit code received by text message, on the sign-in sheet.

signInSheet.phoneCode.autofill.text: The code fills itself in on most phones.
signInSheet.phoneCode.autofill.description: Hint under the text-message code field on the sign-in sheet: most phones offer to enter the code from the message automatically.

signInSheet.phoneCode.submit.description: Button under the text-message code field on the sign-in sheet: checks the code and signs the person in.

signInSheet.phoneCode.checking.description: Shown on that Continue button, disabled, while the text-message code is being checked.

signInSheet.phoneCode.changeNumber.description: Link under the text-message code field: goes back to type a different phone number.

signInSheet.phoneCode.resend.description: Link under the text-message code field: sends another code to the same phone number.

signInSheet.phoneCode.resendIn_one.description: The Send a new code link while it is disabled: counts down the seconds until another text-message code may be asked for. {{count}} is seconds; "s" is the abbreviation for seconds.

signInSheet.phoneCode.resendIn_other.description: The Send a new code link while it is disabled: counts down the seconds until another text-message code may be asked for. {{count}} is seconds; "s" is the abbreviation for seconds.

signInSheet.phoneCode.missing.text: Enter the code from the text
signInSheet.phoneCode.missing.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when Continue was pressed with the text-message code field empty. "The text" is the text message (SMS).

signInSheet.phoneCode.tooManyAttempts.text: Too many code attempts. Try again shortly.
signInSheet.phoneCode.tooManyAttempts.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when wrong text-message codes were entered too many times and the server gave no message of its own.

signInSheet.phoneCode.rejected.description: Error on the sign-in sheet when the text-message code was refused and the server gave no reason of its own.

signInSheet.username.title.description: Title of the sign-in sheet on the step where a new account made with Apple, Google or a phone number chooses its username.

signInSheet.username.lead.text: Your username is public on Homeroom. It is how people @mention you.
signInSheet.username.lead.description: Line under "Pick a username". Homeroom is the product's name; to @mention someone is to write @ and their username in a message.

signInSheet.username.label.description: Label of the username field on the "Pick a username" step of the sign-in sheet.

signInSheet.providerUsernamePlaceholder.text: Letters, numbers and underscores, 3 to 32 characters.
signInSheet.providerUsernamePlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the username field on the "Pick a username" step of the sign-in sheet: what a username may contain and how long it may be.

signInSheet.username.submit.description: Button on the "Pick a username" step of the sign-in sheet: saves the username and finishes signing in.

signInSheet.username.finishing.description: Shown on that Continue button, disabled, while the username is being saved.

signInSheet.username.missing.description: Error on the "Pick a username" step of the sign-in sheet when the field is empty.

signInSheet.username.refused.description: Error on the "Pick a username" step of the sign-in sheet when the server refused the username (taken or not allowed) and gave no reason of its own.

signInSheet.username.expired.description: Error on the "Pick a username" step of the sign-in sheet when too much time passed since signing in with Apple, Google or the phone.

signInSheet.password.title.description: Title of the sign-in sheet on the username and password step.

signInSheet.password.lead.text: With your username or email, and your password.
signInSheet.password.lead.description: Line under the title "Sign in" on the password step of the sign-in sheet; it continues the title's thought.

signInSheet.password.identifierLabel.description: Label of the first field on the password step of the sign-in sheet: either the username or the email address of the account.

signInSheet.password.label.description: Label of the password field on the password step of the sign-in sheet.

signInSheet.password.submit.description: Button on the password step of the sign-in sheet: signs in with the username and password.

signInSheet.password.signingIn.description: Shown on the Sign in button of the sign-in sheet, disabled, while the password is being checked.

signInSheet.password.otherWays.description: Link under the password step of the sign-in sheet, when Apple or Google sign-in is offered: goes back to those buttons.

signInSheet.password.useEmailCode.description: Link under the password step of the sign-in sheet, when only email sign-in is offered: goes to the step that emails a code.

signInSheet.password.forgot.description: Link under the password step of the sign-in sheet: opens the screen for resetting a forgotten password.

signInSheet.account.title.description: Title of the sign-in sheet on the last step of making an account with an email code: choosing a username if there is none yet, and a password if the person wants one.

signInSheet.account.leadWithUsername.text: Pick a username. It is public on Homeroom. A password is optional: without one, you sign in with an emailed code.
signInSheet.account.leadWithUsername.description: Line under the title of the last step of making an account with an email code, when the new account still needs a username. Homeroom is the product's name; an emailed code is a one-time code sent by email.

signInSheet.account.lead.text: Pick a password for next time, or skip it and sign in with an emailed code.
signInSheet.account.lead.description: Line under the title of the last step of making an account with an email code, when the account already has a username and may add a password. An emailed code is a one-time code sent by email.

signInSheet.account.usernameLabel.description: Label of the username field on the "Finish your account" step of the sign-in sheet.

signInSheet.usernamePlaceholder.text: Letters, numbers and underscores, 3 to 32 characters.
signInSheet.usernamePlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the username field on the "Finish your account" step of the sign-in sheet: what a username may contain and how long it may be.

signInSheet.account.passwordLabel.description: Label of the new password field on the "Finish your account" step of the sign-in sheet. The password may be left empty.

signInSheet.account.passwordPlaceholder.description: Placeholder inside the new password field on the "Finish your account" step of the sign-in sheet.

signInSheet.account.submit.description: Button on the "Finish your account" step of the sign-in sheet: saves the username and the password, if one was typed, and finishes.

signInSheet.account.finishing.description: Shown on that Continue button, disabled, while the account is being saved.

signInSheet.account.usernameMissing.description: Error on the "Finish your account" step of the sign-in sheet when the username field is empty.

signInSheet.account.passwordTooShort.text: Password must be at least 8 characters
signInSheet.account.passwordTooShort.description: Error on the "Finish your account" step of the sign-in sheet when the password typed is shorter than 8 characters.

signInSheet.account.failed.text: Could not finish setting up your account
signInSheet.account.failed.description: Error on the "Finish your account" step of the sign-in sheet when the server refused and gave no reason of its own.

waitlist.documentTitle.description: Title of the browser tab while the join-the-waitlist screen is open. Join is a verb.

waitlist.step.email.description: Small upper-case line above the title on the join-the-waitlist screen, before the person has joined. Keep the dot between the two parts.

waitlist.step.joined.description: Small upper-case line on the waitlist screen right after the person joined and before they confirm their email. Keep the dot.

waitlist.step.emailAddress.description: Small upper-case line on the check-your-status flow of the waitlist screen, where a person who already joined asks for a code by email to see their place, on the step that asks for the email address. Keep the dot.

waitlist.step.enterCode.description: Small upper-case line on the check-your-status flow of the waitlist screen, where a person who already joined asks for a code by email to see their place, on the step that asks for the six-digit code. Keep the dot.

waitlist.step.status.description: Small upper-case line on the waitlist screen once the code was accepted in the check-your-status flow: what follows is the person's place on the waitlist.

waitlist.step.done.description: Small upper-case line on the waitlist screen once a new person has joined and confirmed their email: nothing more is required.

waitlist.title.description: Title on the join-the-waitlist screen. Join is a verb.

waitlist.intro.text: Describe the app you want in chat, an AI builds it, and the group votes the changes in.
waitlist.intro.description: First paragraph on the join-the-waitlist screen: how Homeroom works. "The group" is the community that uses the app; to vote a change in is to accept it by voting.

waitlist.points.builtHere.text: Every app in the directory was built here, by the people who use it.
waitlist.points.builtHere.description: First bullet point on the join-the-waitlist screen. "The directory" is Homeroom's list of public apps; "here" is on Homeroom.

waitlist.points.chain.text: They run on the Homeroom chain, and contributors own a share of what they build.
waitlist.points.chain.description: Second bullet point on the join-the-waitlist screen. "They" are the apps; "the Homeroom chain" is Homeroom's own blockchain.

waitlist.points.gradual.text: We're letting people in a few at a time. The public apps are open to everyone now.
waitlist.points.gradual.description: Third bullet point on the join-the-waitlist screen.

waitlist.justEmail.description: Line above the form on the join-the-waitlist screen: only an email address is needed.

waitlist.email.label.description: Label of the required email field on the join-the-waitlist screen.

waitlist.email.hint.text: We only email you when your spot comes up. No newsletter.
waitlist.email.hint.description: Hint under the email field on the join-the-waitlist screen. "Your spot comes up" means it is the person's turn to get access.

waitlist.email.placeholder.description: Example email address shown as the placeholder of the email field on the join-the-waitlist screen. Keep it a valid-looking address at example.com.

waitlist.optional.description: Small grey tag beside a field's label on the join-the-waitlist screen: the field may be left empty.

waitlist.country.label.description: Label of the country drop-down on the join-the-waitlist screen: the country the person lives in.

waitlist.country.hint.text: We’re building early groups across different regions.
waitlist.country.hint.description: Hint under the Country label on the join-the-waitlist screen: why the country is asked.

waitlist.country.placeholder.description: First, unselectable option of the country drop-down on the join-the-waitlist screen.

waitlist.discovery.label.description: Label over a row of chips on the join-the-waitlist screen asking where the person heard about Homeroom.

waitlist.discovery.hint.description: Hint under "How did you find us?": choose the chip that fits best.

waitlist.submit.description: Main button of the form on the join-the-waitlist screen: adds the email address to the waitlist.

waitlist.join.emailMissing.description: Error under the join-the-waitlist form when it was submitted with the email field empty.

waitlist.join.failed.description: Error under the join-the-waitlist form when the server refused and gave no reason of its own.

waitlist.join.network.description: Error under the join-the-waitlist form when the request did not reach the server.

waitlist.alreadyJoined.description: Line under the join-the-waitlist form. <0></0> is a button that opens the flow for seeing one's place on the waitlist.

waitlist.joined.title.description: Heading on the waitlist screen right after a new person joined.

waitlist.joined.titleAgain.description: Heading on the waitlist screen when the person tried to join with an address that had already joined.

waitlist.joined.titleStatus.description: Heading of the check-your-status flow on the waitlist screen.

waitlist.joined.lead.text: Your signup is saved. Next, confirm your email so we can let you know when your spot opens.
waitlist.joined.lead.description: Paragraph under "You're on the waitlist!": the next step is entering the code that was emailed.

waitlist.joined.leadAgain.text: Your spot was already saved, so nothing is lost. This address still needs confirming, so use the code below and we’ll email you when your spot opens.
waitlist.joined.leadAgain.description: Paragraph under "You’re already on the waitlist" when the address had joined before but was never confirmed. "The code below" is the code field under it.

waitlist.joined.leadStatusAddress.text: Enter the address you joined with and we’ll email you a code. It shows where you stand, and confirms your address if it still needs it.
waitlist.joined.leadStatusAddress.description: Paragraph under "Check your status" on the step that asks for the email address. "Where you stand" is the person's place on the waitlist.

waitlist.joined.leadStatusCode.text: This shows where you stand, and confirms your address if it still needs it.
waitlist.joined.leadStatusCode.description: Paragraph under "Check your status" on the step that asks for the code. "This" is entering the code.

waitlist.request.label.description: Label of the email field on the check-your-status flow of the waitlist screen, where a person who already joined asks for a code by email to see their place.

waitlist.request.hint.text: Enter the address you joined with. We will email you a six-digit code.
waitlist.request.hint.description: Hint under the email field of the check-your-status flow.

waitlist.request.placeholder.description: Example email address shown as the placeholder of the email field of the check-your-status flow. Keep it a valid-looking address at example.com.

waitlist.request.submit.description: Button of the check-your-status flow: emails a six-digit code to the address typed.

waitlist.request.sending.description: Shown on the Email me a code button, disabled, while the email is being sent.

waitlist.request.cooldown_one.description: The Email me a code button while it is disabled after a send: counts down the seconds until another code may be asked for. {{count}} is seconds; "s" abbreviates seconds.

waitlist.request.cooldown_other.description: The Email me a code button while it is disabled after a send: counts down the seconds until another code may be asked for. {{count}} is seconds; "s" abbreviates seconds.

waitlist.request.cap.text: You can ask for up to 10 codes a day.
waitlist.request.cap.description: Small note under the Email me a code button: the daily limit of emailed codes.

waitlist.request.haveCode.description: Link under the Email me a code button: skips to the step where the code is typed.

waitlist.request.emailMissing.description: Error in the check-your-status flow when a code was asked for with the email field empty.

waitlist.request.notFound.text: We can’t find that address on the waitlist. Check the spelling, or join with it.
waitlist.request.notFound.description: Error in the check-your-status flow when the address typed never joined the waitlist. A Join the waitlist button appears under it.

waitlist.request.sent.text: If that address is on our waitlist, a six-digit code is on its way.
waitlist.request.sent.description: Confirmation in the check-your-status flow after a code was asked for, when the server sent no message of its own. Worded so it does not reveal whether the address is on the waitlist.

waitlist.request.failed.description: Error in the check-your-status flow when asking for a code failed and the server gave no reason of its own.

waitlist.request.network.description: Error in the check-your-status flow when the request for a code did not reach the server.

waitlist.request.joinInstead.description: Button shown in the check-your-status flow after the address was not found: goes to the join form with that address filled in.

waitlist.confirm.back.description: Link above the code field of the check-your-status flow: returns to the step that asks for the email address. Keep the arrow.

waitlist.confirm.label.description: Label of the six-digit code field on the waitlist screen for a person who has just joined. Keep the dot.

waitlist.confirm.labelStatus.description: Label of the code field in the check-your-status flow of the waitlist screen.

waitlist.confirm.hint.text: Check your email for a six-digit code, and use the newest one. You can also just click the link in it. Codes work for 15 minutes.
waitlist.confirm.hint.description: Hint under the code field on the waitlist screen when the address the code went to is not known. "The newest one" is the newest email; "the link in it" is a confirmation link in that email.

waitlist.confirm.hintSentTo.text: Check {{email}} for a six-digit code, and use the newest email. You can also just click the link in it. Codes work for 15 minutes.
waitlist.confirm.hintSentTo.description: Hint under the code field on the waitlist screen. {{email}} is the address the code was sent to; "the link in it" is a confirmation link in that email.

waitlist.confirm.hintStatus.text: Enter the six-digit code from your email. Codes work for 15 minutes, so if yours has expired, ask for a new one below.
waitlist.confirm.hintStatus.description: Hint under the code field in the check-your-status flow when the person said they already have a code. "Below" points to the Send a new code button.

waitlist.confirm.submit.description: Button beside the six-digit code field on the waitlist screen: checks the code and confirms the email address. A verb.

waitlist.confirm.emailMissing.text: Enter the email address you joined with first.
waitlist.confirm.emailMissing.description: Error on the waitlist screen when a code was submitted but no email address is known for it.

waitlist.confirm.codeMissing.text: Enter the six-digit code from your email.
waitlist.confirm.codeMissing.description: Error on the waitlist screen when Confirm was pressed with the code field empty.

waitlist.confirm.rejected.description: Error on the waitlist screen when the code was refused and the server gave no reason of its own.

waitlist.confirm.network.description: Error on the waitlist screen when the code could not be sent to the server.

waitlist.resend.ready.text: Didn't get it, or has it expired? <0>Send a new code</0> You can ask for up to 10 codes a day.
waitlist.resend.ready.description: Line under the code field on the waitlist screen. <0></0> is the button that emails another six-digit code; the last sentence is the daily limit. "It" is the code.

waitlist.resend.sending.text: Didn't get it, or has it expired? <0>Sending…</0> You can ask for up to 10 codes a day.
waitlist.resend.sending.description: Line under the code field on the waitlist screen. <0></0> is the button that emails another six-digit code; the last sentence is the daily limit. This form is shown while the new code is being sent and the button is disabled.

waitlist.resend.cooldown_one.text: Didn't get it, or has it expired? <0>Send a new code ({{count}}s)</0> You can ask for up to 10 codes a day.
waitlist.resend.cooldown_one.description: Line under the code field on the waitlist screen. <0></0> is the button that emails another six-digit code; the last sentence is the daily limit. This form is shown while the button is disabled after a send; {{count}} counts down the seconds left and "s" abbreviates seconds.

waitlist.resend.cooldown_other.text: Didn't get it, or has it expired? <0>Send a new code ({{count}}s)</0> You can ask for up to 10 codes a day.
waitlist.resend.cooldown_other.description: Line under the code field on the waitlist screen. <0></0> is the button that emails another six-digit code; the last sentence is the daily limit. This form is shown while the button is disabled after a send; {{count}} counts down the seconds left and "s" abbreviates seconds.

waitlist.resend.emailMissing.description: Error under the Send a new code button on the waitlist screen when no email address is known to send to.

waitlist.resend.sent.text: If that address is on our waitlist, a six-digit code is on its way.
waitlist.resend.sent.description: Confirmation under the Send a new code button on the waitlist screen, when the server sent no message of its own. Worded so it does not reveal whether the address is on the waitlist.

waitlist.resend.failed.description: Error under the Send a new code button on the waitlist screen when the server refused and gave no reason of its own.

waitlist.resend.network.description: Error under the Send a new code button on the waitlist screen when the request did not reach the server.

waitlist.status.titleIn.description: Heading of the status panel on the waitlist screen when the person has been given access.

waitlist.status.titleListed.description: Heading of the status panel on the waitlist screen when the email address is confirmed and the person is waiting for access. "The list" is the waitlist.

waitlist.status.leadHasAccount.text: Your account already has access. Sign in any time.
waitlist.status.leadHasAccount.description: Paragraph of the status panel on the waitlist screen when the person has access and already has an account.

waitlist.status.leadAdmitted.text: Access is open for you. Create your account with this address and you’re straight in.
waitlist.status.leadAdmitted.description: Paragraph of the status panel on the waitlist screen when the person has access but no account yet. "This address" is the email address shown below.

waitlist.status.leadWaiting.text: We’re letting people in a few at a time. We’ll email you when yours comes up.
waitlist.status.leadWaiting.description: Paragraph of the status panel on the waitlist screen while the person is still waiting. "Yours" is the person's spot.

waitlist.status.since.description: Line of the status panel on the waitlist screen. {{date}} is the day the person joined the waitlist, already written out in the device's language (for example 3 October 2026).

waitlist.status.registeredWith.description: Line of the status panel on the waitlist screen. {{email}} is the address the person joined with, drawn stronger inside <0></0>.

waitlist.status.signIn.description: Button of the status panel on the waitlist screen for a person who has access and an account: goes to the sign-in screen.

waitlist.status.createAccount.description: Button of the status panel on the waitlist screen for a person who has access but no account: goes to the sign-up screen.

waitlist.more.eyebrow.description: Small upper-case line above the offer of the extra survey, on the waitlist screen's status panel: answering is optional and gives a better place on the waitlist.

waitlist.more.title.description: Heading of the offer of the extra survey on the waitlist screen. "In" means being given access to Homeroom.

waitlist.more.offer.text: Four more questions, about three minutes: the group you’d bring, a tool you’ve lost, where else you are. These are the answers we actually read when we pick who gets in next.
waitlist.more.offer.description: Paragraph of the offer of the extra survey on the waitlist screen, before the person has answered it. The three items after the colon are the survey's topics.

waitlist.more.answered.text: Your answers are saved. Add to them any time, and they merge, so nothing you already wrote is lost.
waitlist.more.answered.description: Paragraph in place of the survey offer on the waitlist screen once the person has answered the extra survey.

waitlist.more.start.description: Button of the survey offer on the waitlist screen: opens the extra survey. "Them" is the four questions.

waitlist.more.edit.description: Button on the waitlist screen once the extra survey was answered: reopens the survey with the answers in it.

waitlist.more.skip.text: Or stop here. You’re on the list either way, and the link is in your email.
waitlist.more.skip.description: Small text beside the survey button on the waitlist screen: answering is not required. "The link" is the link to the survey.

waitlist.queued.text: You're already on the waitlist. We'll email you when your spot opens.
waitlist.queued.description: Shown on the waitlist screen in place of the form to a person who is signed in and still waiting for access.

login.title.description: Heading of the sign-in screen while it shows the username and password form.

login.networkError.description: Error on the sign-in screen when a request did not reach the server.

login.passwordAccount.text: This account signs in with a password. Enter it below to continue.
login.passwordAccount.description: Error above the password form on the sign-in screen, after the person tried an email code or a provider for an account that must use its password. "Below" is the password field.

login.offline.title.description: Heading of the notice on the sign-in screen while the device has no internet connection.

login.offline.body.text: Signing in needs a connection. Your username and password are checked on the server. Reconnect and try again; if you were signed in on this device before, reloading once you're back online will take you straight in.
login.offline.body.description: Body of the offline notice on the sign-in screen.

login.offline.retry.description: Button on the offline notice on the sign-in screen: checks again whether the device is connected.

login.wallet.submit.description: Button on the sign-in screen inside the Homeroom phone app: signs in by approving a signature with the person's crypto wallet instead of typing a password.

login.wallet.or.description: Word in the middle of a horizontal divider on the sign-in screen, between the Sign in with Wallet button and the password form.

login.wallet.verifying.description: Status under the Sign in with Wallet button while the wallet's signature is being requested and checked.

login.wallet.noChallenge.text: Could not get challenge from server
login.wallet.noChallenge.description: Error under the Sign in with Wallet button when the server did not send the text the wallet has to sign.

login.wallet.failed.description: Error under the Sign in with Wallet button when the server refused the wallet's signature and gave no reason of its own.

login.wallet.denied.description: Error under the Sign in with Wallet button when the person declined the signature request in their wallet.

login.wallet.signatureFailed.description: Error under the Sign in with Wallet button when signing failed for another reason. {{reason}} is the technical message from the wallet, shown as it came.

login.identifierLabel.description: Label of the first field of the password form on the sign-in screen: either the username or the email address of the account.
